# Project bootstrap workflow

Bootstrap turns an accepted product contract into a verified foundation. The selected mode changes decision/parallelism behavior, not the required endpoint evidence.

## Contract

Establish or recover:
- outcome/users;
- constraints and non-goals;
- acceptance criteria and definition of done;
- product surfaces;
- runtime/deployment boundary;
- stack/design requirements already decided;
- effects that remain separately gated.

Every mode keeps this opening contract.

## Inspect destination

Before scaffolding:
- inspect the actual directory/Git state;
- preserve existing work and project conventions;
- reuse an existing project when present;
- initialize/reset only when the accepted contract allows it.

## Mode-sensitive setup

- auto: resolve ordinary open choices from evidence/accepted constraints and continue;
- full: surface missing material stack/design decisions;
- fast: combine/reduce research overhead while preserving implementation/review/test gates;
- parallel: form a dependency graph and non-overlapping ownership only when runtime capability supports it honestly.

Do not invent parallelism or ask for decisions already settled.

## Build the foundation

1. Research material open choices at the depth the mode requires.
2. Select and record stack/design decisions that materially affect future work.
3. Produce visual/interface evidence when the product surface needs it.
4. Hand the accepted contract/setup to Cook; do not insert an unnecessary separate plan ceremony.
5. Let Cook size the implementation plan and run its test/review gates.
6. For web surfaces, run UX/AX enhancement when required/available and review its changes.
7. Release/live-verify only when the Contract includes a release target and the concrete provider effects are authorized.
8. Finish documentation/onboarding and reconcile definition of done.

A thin vertical slice can be a useful risk-reduction technique, but it is **not a universal bootstrap endpoint**. Use it when it proves a load-bearing integration assumption before wider build-out.

## Completion

A scaffold, wireframe, build, or isolated happy path is intermediate evidence.

Completion depends on the accepted definition of done, verification, mandatory review, relevant UX/AX evidence, onboarding/configuration path, and authorized delivery endpoint.
